## 1. 当前观察 (observation)

### Scope, units and statistics

- Seeds 3401 (breadth seed; the published ADDENDUM_12 units), 3407 and 3413 (ADDENDUM_03 §1.1 panel rows); `lag_local_tokens`; objective NCE; FAU and DTU; all 5 subject folds × 2 content folds. Expected test identities: ad|dtu 44, ad|fau 67, att|dtu 44, att|fau 67.
- Unit of every Δ: D_ATTENTION 2AFC accuracy difference (proportion; AT-LEVEL is accuracy − 0.5); D_ADAPT `gain_bits` difference in bits per query (query = last 70 % of each test participant's 5 s segments); rank: `rank_pct` is the mean over queries of rank / (n_candidates − 1), a proportion (0 = true candidate ranked first, about 0.5 = chance); Δrank = reference − candidate in the same proportion units (positive = lower rank = better; ×100 = percentile points); top1 as a proportion. Positive = candidate better throughout.
- n counts unique test identities. Per seed and configuration an identity's value is the mean over its units (its two content folds); the identity mean over seeds averages the within-seed paired differences over the seeds in which the pair exists. Seeds, folds and content folds never add n.
- Intervals: bootstrap-t over identities (B = 4,000); [sim.] = simultaneous 95 % by max-t within the panel family (each ADDENDUM_12 family restricted to its panel members, the same member set for every seed). In a one-member family (AT-TASK, AD-GAIN, AD-SUPPORT) the simultaneous interval equals the pointwise bootstrap-t interval, so there is no multiplicity control across windows, datasets or support levels (§1.14 adds it across windows and support levels as a post hoc sensitivity). Replicate indices depend only on family label and metric, so the three seeds and the identity mean resample the same identities. Classes (I>0 / I<0 / contains 0) describe the simultaneous interval of the declared draws; §1.13 shows how stable they are under alternative draws. No p-values.
- The intervals condition on the fitted models. The between-seed range is the only direct view of training randomness here, and three seeds give a coarse one (it also contains seed-dependent readout and probe sampling).

### 1.12 Between-seed spread against the per-seed simultaneous widths (primary readout; descriptive)

## 2. 当前工作判断 (working interpretation)

These are working judgements for this recipe only: `lag_local_tokens`, NCE, FAU and DTU, and the same 67 + 44 test identities.
They are not final conclusions. Sections 2–4, 6 and 7 are written by hand after the generated tables had been viewed. Version 1
of sections 2–4 and 6 was written between the generation at 20:01 and 20:03:46 CEST (file mtime). Version 2 of sections 2, 3
and 7 (this text; the changes are listed in section 7) was written after the version-2 tables (generated 20:48 CEST) had been
viewed; the file's modification time marks its end.

1. **Personal supervised adaptation (card contrast none → input_spatial).** Seeds 3407 and 3413 reproduce the direction of the
   seed-3401 estimate in all four cells, and roughly its size.
   - At 30 % support the input map raises unified query gain in every seed (each I>0). Identity means: FAU +0.245
     [+0.141, +0.349] and DTU +0.216 [+0.112, +0.320] bits per query. Both stay I>0 with max-t across the two support levels
     (§1.14).
   - At 10 % support on DTU it lowers unified gain in every seed: −0.154 / −0.174 / −0.186, each I<0. The identity mean is
     −0.171 [−0.275, −0.068], and −0.171 [−0.288, −0.055] with max-t across the support levels. Unified rank and top1 move the
     same way: identity-mean Δrank −0.024 [−0.035, −0.013] (a rank proportion, i.e. −2.4 percentile points) and Δtop1 −0.008
     [−0.015, −0.001].
   - At 10 % support on FAU the estimate is positive in every seed (+0.064 … +0.100). The identity-mean interval
     [−0.006, +0.171] contains 0, so no benefit is resolved.
   - At seed 3401 this FAU 10 % cell is I>0 [+0.0005, +0.1668] in the one-member panel family but "contains 0"
     [−0.0106, +0.1779] in the published two-member family (D_ADAPT_RESULTS.md). The estimate and the pointwise interval are the
     same; only the critical value differs. The panel-family class sits at the Monte-Carlo margin: it is I>0 in 29 of the 50
     alternative draw sets (sim_low −0.0052 … +0.0029; §1.13) and in 4 of the verifier's 20 independent redraws, while the
     published family stays "contains 0" in 50/50. With max-t across the support levels it contains 0 (§1.14). It is not
     evidence of a seed-3401 benefit.
   - Moving from 10 % to 30 % support helps in every seed. Identity means: FAU +0.162 [+0.132, +0.193], DTU +0.388
     [+0.320, +0.456].
   - The between-seed spreads are 0.013–0.074 bits. Every one is below every per-seed simultaneous width (widths 0.065–0.271
     bits; §1.12). In this recipe, differences between people dominate the uncertainty, not the training seed.
2. **The negative DTU 10 % cell is a statement about the unified readout.**
   - Unified gain is I<0 in all three seeds (above).
   - Native gain for the same cell is unresolved: +0.229 [−0.065, +0.523] / −0.009 [−0.230, +0.212] / +0.231 [−0.067, +0.529]
     (pointwise), identity mean +0.150 [−0.110, +0.411]. It is positive in two seeds and about 0 in seed 3407, and no native
     interval excludes 0.
   - So what holds in all three seeds is unified I<0 with native unresolved. Version 1 described this as a disagreement between
     the readouts that "reproduces across seeds"; it does not (section 7).
   - "input_spatial at 10 % support lowers query gain" therefore applies to the unified readout, which was fitted with the frozen
     base model. It is no evidence that personal adaptation cannot help.
3. **Attention training task (card contrast attended_alignment → alignment_plus_selection, NCE).**
   - In every seed, window and dataset, unified mean_score 2AFC accuracy changes by at most 0.011.
   - Identity means: FAU +0.003 / +0.006 / +0.005 and DTU −0.002 / −0.004 / −0.002 at 5 / 10 / 20 s.
   - One of the six identity-mean cells excludes 0: FAU 10 s, +0.0060 [+0.0004, +0.0117], in a one-member family.
     - It keeps that class in 50/50 alternative draws, so it is not a draw artefact.
     - With max-t across the three FAU windows it is +0.0060 [−0.0007, +0.0127] and contains 0 (§1.14).
     - Per seed it is I>0 only at 3413: +0.0107 [+0.0020, +0.0195]; with max-t across windows [+0.0002, +0.0213], which is I>0
       in 20 of 50 alternative draws. At 3401 and 3407 it contains 0.
   - Over three seeds every identity-mean interval lies within −0.011 … +0.012 accuracy. No recipe difference larger than about
     0.01 is supported, and equivalence was not tested.
   - The native accuracy (a secondary readout, kept separate) leans positive on FAU: identity means +0.010 / +0.025 / +0.036 at
     5 / 10 / 20 s, pointwise intervals excluding 0. On DTU it is about 0.
4. **AT-LEVEL and AT-LENGTH hold in every seed.**
   - Above-chance 2AFC and the gain from longer windows: 20/20 members are I>0 in each seed and for the identity mean.
   - All 80 of these cells keep their class in 50/50 alternative draws. The closest to the margin is AT-LENGTH FAU attended
     5 → 10 s at 3413 (sim_low +0.0004), which was I>0 in 19 of the verifier's 20 redraws.
   - Between-seed spreads are at most 0.0142 (AT-LEVEL FAU attended 20 s), and each is below every per-seed simultaneous width
     (§1.12).
   - The dataset magnitudes stay apart and are not pooled. For example, the 20 s attended identity means are FAU +0.095 and
     DTU +0.337.
   - Window length is a question of evidence integration, not of latency or recording budget.
5. **AT-INTEGRATOR cannot be interpreted yet.**
   - Under the legacy candidate order, same-model integrator differences change sign between seeds at 5 s. For FAU attended
     they are −0.005 / +0.009 / −0.006, and each per-seed interval excludes 0 in its own direction.
   - At 10 / 20 s the FAU differences are mostly negative, but they vary between seeds by up to 0.046.
   - The between-seed variation is often far larger than the within-seed identity intervals (§1.12):
     - above every per-seed simultaneous width in 8 of 12 members;
     - between the narrowest and the widest width in 1 (DTU attended 10 s: 0.0077 against 0.0063–0.0096);
     - below every width in 3 (DTU attended 20 s, DTU align+sel 10 s and 20 s);
     - the largest ratio is FAU attended 5 s: spread 0.0147 against widths 0.0028–0.0034, 4.4–5.3-fold.
   - That variation includes the seed-dependent fit of the learned integrator.
   - One class is at the Monte-Carlo margin: DTU attended 5 s at 3413, I>0 [+0.0000, +0.0037], kept in 47 of 50 alternative draws.
   - The pattern is what a fitted threshold would produce if it should be 0 by symmetry but is not, while every test window
     carries label 1. This is the candidate-order problem; R34_ATTENTION_ORDER has not tested it yet.
   - No AT-INTEGRATOR row should be read as an integrator comparison before that correction.
   - The native learned_temporal column stays degenerate and seed-dependent (FAU attended 20 s: −0.362 / −0.629 / +0.016).

## 3. 仍竞争的解释 (competing explanations)

- **DTU 10 % harm against the 30 % benefit.** The present design does not separate these four explanations:
  - (a) An under-determined C × C map: C² parameters, fitted from the support set. At 10 % support a DTU participant-unit block
    has 4–9 five-second support segments (median 7); FAU has 9–12 (median 10.5). At 30 %: DTU 11–28 (median 22), FAU 28–35
    (median 31.5) (§1.9).
  - (b) The step count is chosen on the training side and then applied to both support fractions. It is chosen on up to 8
    training participants' early-stopping segments, with a 30 % support split and the native gain (`run_adapt3`). The largest
    of the candidates 20 / 50 / 100, 100 steps, was chosen in 25/30 DTU cells (8, 7 and 10 per seed) and in 25/30 FAU cells
    (8, 8 and 9).
  - (c) The adapted representation drifts away from the unified bridge fitted with the base model, while native alignment
    improves. This predicts native gain above 0 where unified gain is below 0. Native is positive in two seeds and about 0 in
    the third, and every native interval includes 0, so the data neither support nor exclude (c). Version 1 said (c) "fits the
    opposite native sign" (section 7).
  - (d) Dataset differences, such as recording length or channel layout. Not examined here.
- **FAU groups at 30 % support** (identity means, descriptive): CI +0.448, HA +0.147, TH +0.098.
  - A larger adaptation gain where the base readout is weakest may only mean there is more room to improve.
  - This is not a group contrast, and no method is chosen by it.
- **Near-zero task contrast.**
  - (a) Selection supervision may add little beyond alignment for these local models.
  - (b) The comparison is between two recipes, not a pure selection effect. The selection weight was chosen on the training
    side: 1.0 in 7/10 FAU cells in every seed, and in 8–9/10 DTU cells.
  - (c) The unified bridge is fitted on single-speaker segments and may not express a change in selection. The only hint of
    this is the FAU native lean, which is a secondary readout.
- **Learned integrator.** Three explanations remain open, and only the order-corrected re-evaluation separates them:
  - an order artefact (intercept or threshold);
  - a real disadvantage of the 5-summary logistic integrator;
  - a mismatch between training and test windows.
- **Scope of the uncertainty.**
  - Every interval is conditional on the fitted models.
  - Spread versus width, with one rule for every family (§1.12):
    - in AD-GAIN, AD-SUPPORT, AT-TASK, AT-LEVEL and AT-LENGTH the between-seed spread is below every per-seed simultaneous
      width (32/32 members);
    - in AT-INTEGRATOR it is above every width in 8 of 12 members, between in 1 and below every width in 3. At most it is 5.3
      times the narrowest width (FAU attended 5 s).
  - Monte-Carlo error of the intervals themselves (B = 4,000): two of the 176 panel cells and one of the 40 card-family cells
    change class under alternative draws (§1.13). Their classes are reported as declared but read as lying at the margin.
  - Multiplicity: the one-member panel families give no control across windows, datasets or support levels. With max-t across
    windows or support levels within a dataset (§1.14, post hoc), only two classes change, and every other card-contrast class
    is unchanged:
    - for the identity mean, AT-TASK FAU 10 s (I>0 → contains 0);
    - per seed, AD-GAIN FAU 10 % at 3401 (I>0 → contains 0).
  - Three seeds sample training randomness coarsely: a fourth seed can fall outside the observed range.
  - The panel reuses the same people and contents, so a stable result here is not an independent replication.

## 4. 下一轮干预 (next intervention)

1. **R34_ATTENTION_ORDER** (a separate track, already authorised).
   - Re-score learned_temporal with a paired order swap or antisymmetric scoring, on the same test windows.
   - Use saved per-window scores where they exist, and checkpoints otherwise.
   - Then rerun this module's AT-INTEGRATOR rows on the corrected records. The legacy rows stay in this report.
2. **D_ADAPT true-query R** (a new exploratory evaluation).
   - The current records cannot provide it.
   - All 60 frozen D_ADAPT bases (20 per seed) are present on disk.
   - An evaluation-only rerun of the adaptation, under a new execution version, could store the true and mismatched query
     logloss per participant.
   - The adapters were not saved and have to be refitted, so this needs a GPU.
   - Not run here. No runner for it exists yet, so there is no command to report.
3. **Restricted spatial adapters** (package docs/04 §C; E34_ADAPT_READY).
   - Diagonal, rank-4 low-rank and full spatial maps, with the same 10 %/30 % support and the fixed last-70 % query.
   - Each with ordinary group training and with episode training, using the same adapter.
   - Step selection per support fraction, on the training side.
   - Unified and native reported separately.
   - The concrete observation behind this is the DTU 10 % unified harm, which appears in all three seeds.
4. **No automatic extension.** CS_SINGLE, output_low_rank, selection_only and D_COVERAGE stay seed-3401-only. Whether they get
   seed panels is a question of resource priority, not a performance gate.

## 5. 复用与运行 (reuse and execution)

- Reused: 500 completed unit records — 240 panel records (seeds 3407/3413), 120 distinct seed-3401 panel counterparts (each named by one 3407 and one 3413 row as `reference_3401_id`; the analysis note's "240/240" counts those references), and 140 other seed-3401 lag_local records (D_ATTENTION mean_score rows of the CS_SINGLE and selection_only tasks, D_ADAPT CS_SINGLE and output_low_rank rows), read only for the reproduction check. New jobs: none. GPU: none.
- Run: 60 s wall time in the session's own 2-CPU allocation (nice 10), including the 50-draw Monte-Carlo table and the determinism re-computation; measured peak resident memory 442 MiB (ru_maxrss of this process).
- Determinism: a second computation in the same process (same inputs, without the Monte-Carlo table) reproduced 7472 numbers of the non-meta outputs (max |Δ| 0.0e+00, 0 mismatches) and 27972 numbers of the per-identity file (max |Δ| 0.0e+00, 0 mismatches). Replicate indices depend only on family label, metric and `sci_r1.stats.SEED`.
- Version 1: compared number by number with version 1 (archived in `private/auditory_alignment_v3/aln34/d_multiseed/v1_20261016T2003`): JSON 6818 numbers, max |Δ| 0.0e+00, 0 mismatches, 176 added fields; per-identity file 27972 numbers, max |Δ| 0.0e+00, 0 mismatches.
- True-query risk R for D_ADAPT is not in the records (they store gain_bits, rank_pct, top1 and n_query per participant, support fraction and readout, plus n_support; there is no true-query logloss), so no R table is given. Frozen same-fold bases present for an evaluation-only GPU rerun under a new execution version: 60 of 60.
- Outputs (all 0600): `results/auditory_alignment_v3/aln34/d_multiseed/d_multiseed.json`; this document; the private per-identity values in `private/auditory_alignment_v3/aln34/d_multiseed/per_identity.json`.
- Code: `auditory_alignment_v3/aln34/d_multiseed.py`. Synthetic tests: `tests/auditory_alignment_v3/aln34/test_d_multiseed.py`.

## Not in the panel — these must not share a three-seed statement

These configurations exist for seed 3401 only. The ADDENDUM_12 tables (D_ATTENTION_RESULTS.md, D_ADAPT_RESULTS.md) report them, but the three-seed statements of this document do not cover them.

- every CS_SINGLE cell (D_ATTENTION and D_ADAPT)
- output_low_rank (D_ADAPT)

- AT-TASK 'align->align+sel CS'

- per-segment 5 s attention_2afc (not aggregated at 3401 either)

- **Version 1.**

    JSON, per-identity file, code and tests, and the analysis note as of 19:47.
- **Review.** An independent verifier recomputed v1 from the unit records with its own numpy code (no project import). It
  reproduced exactly the 4,504 JSON numbers and the 792 generated table cells of §1.1–1.8 and §1.10 that it compared, plus the
  rows of the §1.9 coverage tables, and found no numeric error. It reported the problems corrected below.
- **Version 2.**
  - Before any v2 addition was computed, the analysis note received a dated correction section (written 20:34–20:36 CEST). That
    section lists what had been seen by then, including the verifier's Monte-Carlo redraws.
  - The generated sections come from `d_multiseed.py` sha256 a6beabfe38e6, run at 20:48 CEST. Sections 2, 3 and 7 were then
    rewritten by hand; sections 4 and 6 are unchanged from v1.
  - Every v1 number is unchanged (§5: 6,818 JSON numbers and the per-identity file, max |Δ| 0).
- **Corrections, v1 → v2.**
  1. **Rank unit.**
     - v1 wrote "rank in rank-percentile points", "unified rank %" and "−0.024 rank-percentile points".
     - `rank_pct` is a proportion: rank / (n_candidates − 1), 0 = first, about 0.5 = chance. So −0.024 is −2.4 percentile points.
     - Fixed in the generated scope and table labels and in §2.1.
  2. **Native versus unified, DTU 10 %.**
     - v1 §2.2 said the disagreement "reproduces across seeds", and v1 §3(c) said (c) "fits the opposite native sign".
     - In fact native gain is positive in two seeds and about 0 at 3407, and no native interval excludes 0. What holds in all
       three seeds is unified I<0 with native unresolved.
     - Rewritten in §2.2 and §3(c).
  3. **Spread versus width.**
     - v1 used two rules: "smaller than every width" for the 32/32 members, but "larger than the narrowest width" for
       AT-INTEGRATOR (9/12).
     - With one symmetric rule, AT-INTEGRATOR has 8 members above every width, 1 between (DTU attended 10 s) and 3 below every
       width.
     - Now generated in §1.12; §2.5 and §3 cite it.
  4. **Rounding.** "spreads ≤ 0.014" is now ≤ 0.0142 (the largest is 0.01418).
  5. **Rendering.** The D_ATTENTION rows of the coverage table had an unescaped `|`, which shifted their cells. Fixed with `·`; a
     test now checks every table row against its header.
  6. **Provenance.**
     - v1's header said §5 was generated, but its last bullets (determinism, outputs, code) and the paragraph under "Not in the
       panel" were added by hand.
     - The hand-written time "20:00–20:05" should have read 20:01–20:03:46.
     - "Peak memory well under 1 GB" was a fixed string, not a measurement.
     - v2 generates all of §5 and that paragraph, runs and reports the determinism check, and measures peak memory (442 MiB).
  7. **Monte-Carlo margin.**
     - v1 said the seed-3401 change of AD-GAIN FAU 10 % to I>0 comes "only" from the one-member panel family.
     - That holds for the declared draws, but the class depends on the draw: I>0 in 29/50 of our alternative draw sets and 4/20
       of the verifier's.
     - §1.10, §1.13 and §2.1 now say so.
- **Added in v2.** All exploratory and declared in the note before they were computed; the verifier's report had already shown
  some of their values.
  - Per-seed pointwise intervals of the secondary readouts (§1.7).
  - D_ADAPT support and query sizes (§1.9).
  - Spread versus width (§1.12).
  - Monte-Carlo stability of the classes (§1.13).
  - Card-contrast families (§1.14).

- **The two redraw sets give different counts.**
  - For AD-GAIN FAU 10 % at 3401, our 50 alternative draw sets give I>0 in 29/50; the verifier's 20 give 4/20. The two use
    different alternative seeds.
  - An independent numpy recomputation of our 50 sets reproduced 29/50 and the bounds exactly.
  - Both counts say the class depends on the draw. Neither is used to choose a class.
